metadata.title: AI Core

props.name: capability
props.remarks: AI Core capability for identifying, scoping, and governing artificial intelligence systems, including agentic and interconnected AI.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Artificial intelligence, machine learning, autonomous agents, and research AI platforms.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Defines the foundational scope, trust boundaries, and threat context for AI systems.

props.name: threat-framework
props.remarks: Used to model traditional adversarial activity targeting AI infrastructure, supply chains, platforms, and deployment environments.

props.name: threat-framework
props.remarks: Used to model AI‑specific adversarial behaviors including model manipulation, data poisoning, prompt injection, and agentic misuse.

props.name: ai-threat-class
props.remarks: Threats in which AI training or fine-tuning data is poisoned, manipulated, or backdoored to alter downstream behavior.

props.name: ai-threat-class
props.remarks: Threats exploiting inference-time inputs, context, or tool invocation to bypass controls or alter AI behavior.

props.name: ai-threat-class
props.value: Model Extraction and Intellectual Property Theft
props.remarks: Threats involving unauthorized reconstruction of model behavior, parameters, or sensitive training data through querying.

props.name: ai-threat-class
props.remarks: Threats where AI produces plausible but incorrect, misleading, or overconfident outputs that cause downstream harm.

props.name: ai-threat-class
props.remarks: Threats arising from agentic AI acting beyond authorized scope or humans over-relying on AI decisions.

props.name: ai-threat-class
props.remarks: Threats caused by agent-to-agent delegation, transitive trust, or error amplification across AI systems.

props.name: ai-threat-class
props.value: Semantic Data Leakage and Privacy Inference
props.remarks: Threats where sensitive information is revealed indirectly through AI-generated content or inference.

props.name: ai-threat-class
props.remarks: Threats involving repurposing of AI capabilities for harm, misuse of research outputs, or cost and resource exhaustion.

metadata.remarks: AI Core establishes the definition, scope, trust boundaries, and foundational threat model for artificial intelligence systems. It rationalizes the existence of the AI trust plane by explicitly enumerating AI-native threat classes that cannot be adequately addressed by traditional application, data, or SDLC security patterns.

components.title: AI System Identification
components.description: Identification and inventory of AI models, services, agents, and supporting systems.

implemented-requirements.remarks: All AI models, services, and agents are identified, catalogued, and associated with accountable owners.

components.title: Intended Use and Scope
components.description: Definition of approved purposes, limitations, and prohibited uses of AI systems.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Each AI system has a documented intended use, scope, and explicit prohibited uses.

components.title: Trust Boundary Definition
components.description: Definition of trust boundaries between humans, AI models, agents, tools, and external systems.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Trust boundaries are explicitly defined to constrain AI autonomy, tool usage, and inter-system interaction.
